answers.reasonable_increase: For both covered units, the defensible 'reasonable and normal' increase today is the annual allowable 1.6% (Unit 1: $63.92 → $4,058.92; Unit 2: $50.40 → $3,200.40), once per 12 months, on/after the anniversary, with proper 30-day notice, a Housing Inventory report and a rent increase license. Larger banked amounts (Unit 2 only, up to 13.1% / $412.65 / $3,562.65) are lawful ONLY after full verification of the no-increase history and the 24-month banking rule, and require a 90-day notice and itemized banking disclosure.
answers.one_or_both: Raise both units with the same method and percentage (uniform 1.6%), or raise neither — see fairness.html. Different treatment is legally possible only on documented, objective, non-protected-class grounds (e.g., verified banking differences) and is harder to defend under tenant-lawyer review; uniform treatment is the recommended course.
answers.ss_pass_tenant_review: A 1.6% uniform increase with correct notice, license and records satisfies the elements any SF tenant lawyer would check. A >10% banked increase without bulletproof documentation would not.
